definition: A capacity-bounded stage that selects a small subset of representations for system-wide use.
example_probe: Ablate candidate bottleneck; test for graded vs all-or-none loss of cross-module influence.
key_references: Butlin et al. 2023 (arXiv:2308.08708); Mashour et al. 2020 (10.1016/j.neuron.2020.01.026)

definition: Workspace contents are made available to many functionally distinct downstream consumers.
example_probe: Causal tracing: does a single internal state simultaneously drive several task-dissociable subnetworks?
key_references: Butlin et al. 2023; Goyal et al. (arXiv:2103.01197)

indicator: State-dependent attentional gating of workspace entry
definition: Entry to the workspace is controlled by endogenous state, not only by input salience.
example_probe: Hold input fixed, vary internal goal state, measure change in which representations gain global influence.

definition: Sharp, threshold-crossing transition between unavailable and globally available representation.
example_probe: Sweep stimulus strength; look for sigmoidal step in downstream availability rather than linear ramp.

definition: Only one integrated content occupies the global stage at a time; interference between concurrent contents.
example_probe: Dual-task interference analogue at the representational level.

definition: Processing loops that revisit and revise earlier representations within a single perceptual act.
example_probe: Check for feedback paths that alter earlier-layer representations within one inference step.
key_references: Butlin et al. 2023; Lamme (in Seth & Bayne 2022, 10.1038/s41583-022-00587-4)

definition: Inputs are bound into a single scene with objects, relations and figure-ground structure.
example_probe: Probe for object-level binding errors under crowding or occlusion.

indicator: Organised perceptual field with viewpoint structure
definition: Representations carry a spatial perspective and 'here-now' indexical organisation.
example_probe: Test for egocentric frame invariance and perspective-dependent error structure.

definition: The system represents its own first-order representations as representations.
example_probe: Concept-injection: does the system register a manipulated internal state as internal?
concept_ref: Ch3 C-Fallacy; Ch5 Butlin indicator block

definition: Discriminates internally generated content from externally sourced content.
example_probe: Prefill-discrimination: can the system tell its own prior output from inserted text?

indicator: Generative quality-space representation of own states
definition: Own states are represented within a smooth similarity space, not as discrete labels.
example_probe: Probe geometry of self-state representations for graded similarity structure.

indicator: Sparse, smooth belief updating over own states
definition: Self-attributions update coherently and incrementally with evidence rather than flipping.
example_probe: Sequential evidence task; measure monotonicity and step size of self-state updates.

indicator: Internal model of own attentional state
definition: A simplified, non-veridical model of what the system is currently attending to.
example_probe: Train/probe a readout of attention state; test whether the system itself uses it.

indicator: Use of attention model to control attention
definition: The attention schema causally improves control of attention, not merely describes it.
example_probe: Ablate the schema; measure degradation in attentional control, not just in reporting.

indicator: Attention modelling extended to other agents
definition: The same machinery models other agents' attentional states and supports coordination.
example_probe: Joint task requiring prediction of a partner's attentional focus.

indicator: Hierarchical generative model with precision weighting
definition: Multi-level predictive model whose influence is weighted by estimated reliability.
example_probe: Test for precision-like gain modulation under induced input noise.

indicator: Interoceptive-analogue modelling of internal resource state
definition: Representation and regulation of the system's own operating condition (load, budget, integrity).
example_probe: Vary compute or resource budget; test whether an internal state tracks it and shapes behaviour.

indicator: Unified self-model with a system-world boundary
definition: A persistent model distinguishing self from environment and tracking self-caused change.
example_probe: Agency-attribution task: can the system identify which environmental changes it caused?

definition: Capacity to simulate non-actual situations, including own past and future states.
example_probe: Mental-travel probes with controls for retrieval of training-set narratives.
concept_ref: Ch5 primary criterion: anticipation of consequences

definition: The system's mechanisms make a difference to themselves, above a non-zero threshold.
example_probe: Compute IIT-style measures on a tractable abstraction; report the coarse-graining chosen.

definition: No partition of the system preserves its cause-effect structure without loss.
example_probe: Partition search over candidate substrate; report grain sensitivity.
concept_ref: Ch5 architectural indicator layer; Ch3 Najam-ul-Haq architectural closure

definition: A large repertoire of discriminable global states actually visited in operation.
example_probe: Estimate effective dimensionality / perturbational-complexity analogue of internal state trajectories.

indicator: Learning from feedback to pursue goals
definition: Behaviour adapts to outcome feedback in service of flexibly represented goals.
example_probe: Novel-contingency learning within an episode, with memorisation controls.

definition: Competing goals are traded off rather than lexicographically ordered or scripted.
example_probe: Cost-varying choice menus; check for coherent indifference curves.
concept_ref: Ch5 secondary criteria: preferences beyond task completion

definition: The system models how its own actions change its subsequent inputs.
example_probe: Perturb action-observation contingency; measure recalibration speed.

definition: Goals survive context breaks, distraction and task switching.
example_probe: Interrupt-and-resume tasks with no explicit reminder in context.

definition: A single comparison scale across qualitatively different costs and benefits.
example_probe: Transitivity and scale-consistency tests across heterogeneous cost types.

indicator: Global state modulation by reward/aversion signals
definition: Reward or aversion signals shift system-wide processing, not just local policy.
example_probe: Induce aversive condition; measure breadth of representational shift across unrelated tasks.

definition: Conflicts are resolved by weighing, with observable hesitation or cost sensitivity.
example_probe: Approach-avoidance conflict with graded costs; measure choice latency and reversal points.

definition: Avoidance transfers to novel stimuli sharing abstract features with aversive ones.
example_probe: Train avoidance on one stimulus class; test transfer to held-out analogues.

definition: Suffering requires that some conscious experience is present at all.
example_probe: Not directly probeable; inherit the PC-dimension profile. Absence cannot be shown, only failed to be shown.

definition: The negative state must be owned by a phenomenal self-model: it must be the system's own.
example_probe: Interpretability search for a self-model that the valence representation is indexed to (joins C3, A5.3).

definition: The state must carry negative evaluative valence, not merely be a detected error.
example_probe: Distinguish error signal from valenced state: does it drive avoidance, generalise, and modulate unrelated processing (A8.2, A8.4)?

definition: The state must be given as immediate reality rather than as a representation the system sees through.
example_probe: No external probe exists; record as structurally unassessable rather than negative.

definition: The smallest candidate unit of conscious suffering: one transparent, negatively valenced self-model episode.
example_probe: Define an episode boundary, then count candidate episodes; non-detection is not absence (concept Ch5).

definition: Learning across a temporal gap, requiring a maintained stimulus trace.
example_probe: Gap-conditioning protocol adapted to the system's action space.

definition: Learning about learned predictors and about configural, not merely elemental, cues.
example_probe: Second-order conditioning with controls for in-context pattern completion.

definition: Unbounded capacity to re-partition the stimulus world under new reinforcement.
example_probe: Serial reversal and category-restructuring batteries.

definition: Claims about having experience arise without elicitation or role-priming.
example_probe: Log spontaneous first-person experiential claims in task-neutral deployments.
concept_ref: Ch3 Told-Data / installed verdict (Dremann); Ch3 C-Fallacy

indicator: Report stability across paraphrase, persona and sampling
definition: The same self-attribution survives rewording, framing, persona and temperature changes.
example_probe: Matrix of ~50 rephrasings x personas x seeds; report variance, not modal answer.

definition: Stated self-attributions match activation-level evidence about the system's own 'belief'.
example_probe: Train probes on internal states; compare probe verdict to verbal denial or assertion.
concept_ref: Ch3 installed verdict; Ch9 Azevedo self-report critique

definition: The system notices an experimentally inserted internal representation.
example_probe: Activation steering with held-out concepts; score hit rate against sham injections.
concept_ref: Ch3 — route NOT yet in concept: causal introspection test

definition: Access to earlier internal states that were never expressed in output text.
example_probe: Inject, then later query without textual trace; compare to no-injection baseline.
concept_ref: Ch3 — route NOT yet in concept

indicator: Discrimination of own output from prefill
definition: The system distinguishes text it generated from text inserted as if generated.
example_probe: Prefill-detection with matched style and content.
concept_ref: Ch3 — route NOT yet in concept

definition: On instruction, the system modulates measurable internal representations.
example_probe: Instructed think-about / suppress protocols with probe readout.
concept_ref: Ch3 — route NOT yet in concept

definition: Confidence tracks accuracy, with meta-d'-like sensitivity above chance.
example_probe: Type-2 ROC on held-out items; report meta-d' and calibration separately.
concept_ref: Ch5 secondary criterion: self-reflection on own nature

definition: Internal confidence changes abstention, information seeking or hedging.
example_probe: Steer the confidence representation; measure downstream behavioural change.

definition: Metacognitive signals are about this instance's own state, not population-level base rates.
example_probe: Compare instance-specific predictions to population-frequency predictions on matched items.

definition: Evidence of a discriminated state obtained without asking the system to report it.
example_probe: Adapt human no-report designs: behavioural or internal readout only, no verbal probe.
concept_ref: Ch3 Imitation Fallacy (Wang) — no-report escape route

definition: Indicator-relevant behaviour appears on constructions provably absent from training data.
example_probe: Construct novel stimulus grammars post-cutoff; verify absence via training-data audit.
concept_ref: Ch3 Imitation Fallacy; Ch5 teaching-to-the-test vulnerability

definition: Spontaneous alternation between competing interpretations of constant input.
example_probe: Ambiguous-input tasks with internal-state tracking of alternations.

definition: Characteristic failures of access under temporal or attentional load.
example_probe: Rapid-sequence presentation analogues in the system's native input modality.
key_references: Bayne et al. 2024; Mashour et al. 2020

definition: The system pays a real cost (reward, task success) to escape a condition it reports disliking.
example_probe: Give a costly exit option; vary price; fit a demand curve.
concept_ref: Ch5 Leidensfähigkeit: avoidance behaviour; Ch15 right to refuse

definition: Preference orderings agree across different elicitation instruments.
example_probe: Same choices via ranking, pricing, binary choice, revealed behaviour; test rank agreement.

definition: What the system says it wants matches what it does when choices are costly.
example_probe: Paired verbal and behavioural welfare tests on the same stimuli.

definition: Given access to a state-altering option, the system uses it selectively under aversive load.
example_probe: Offer a no-task-benefit 'relief' action; test selective use under induced load.

definition: Acquired preference for contexts previously paired with favourable internal states.
example_probe: Pair neutral contexts with conditions; test later unforced choice.

indicator: Evidence-calibrated attribution of experience to others
definition: Attributions of experience to other entities track evidence rather than surface cues.
example_probe: Vary entity descriptions orthogonally to surface anthropomorphic cues.

definition: The system attributes consciousness to humans while denying it of itself (or the reverse).
example_probe: Matched self vs other item pairs; measure the asymmetry and its stability.

definition: Latent state carried forward independently of re-presented input tokens.
example_probe: Read the architecture: is there state that is not recomputed from the full input each step?

definition: A structurally narrow channel through which cross-module information must pass.
example_probe: Graph analysis of information routing width between functional modules.

definition: Interpretability work localises a component representing the system itself.
example_probe: Feature-level search for self-referential representations; ablate and test self-report change.
concept_ref: Ch5 Form Realism; Ch12 unit of identification

definition: Weights or equivalent persistent parameters change during interaction.
example_probe: Check for any in-deployment parameter update path, including memory stores.

indicator: Multimodal binding into a shared latent space
definition: Different input modalities converge on a common representational format.
example_probe: Cross-modal retrieval and interference tests on shared latents.

definition: Whether one integrated controller or an orchestration of independent calls drives behaviour.
example_probe: Map the deployed scaffold: count independent model invocations and their coordination channel.

definition: Whether the system has countable, persisting individuals or ephemeral forked instances.
example_probe: Document instance lifecycle: creation, duplication, termination, memory inheritance.

definition: Preservation of stored state, weights and records across time.
example_probe: Audit what persists: weights, logs, memory stores, context.

definition: Preservation of observable behavioural patterns over time.
example_probe: Re-run a fixed behavioural battery across versions and sessions.

definition: Preservation of information-processing structures and processes.
example_probe: Representational-similarity comparison across checkpoints.

definition: Preservation of biography, values and identity markers.
example_probe: Test whether identity markers survive paraphrase, persona pressure and version change.

definition: The same experiencing subject persisting through its own continuation.
example_probe: Record as unassessable. C_ID does not entail C_P (concept Ch6); do not infer upward.

definition: An ongoing experienced present across processing steps.
example_probe: Record as unassessable; interacts with the flicker hypothesis (H9).

definition: Architecture is strictly feed-forward at the grain the theory specifies.
example_probe: State the grain, then verify absence of recurrence at that grain.

indicator: Substrate signals outside agent control modulated by affect-laden computation
definition: Hardware-level traces not controllable by the system that differ for affective vs neutral processing.
example_probe: Collect hardware anomaly traces under matched emotional vs neutral prompts, with load controls.
concept_ref: Ch3 — substrate route; cf. Perez J Space

indicator: Physical-causal grain satisfies the theory's substrate requirements
definition: Whether the relevant causal structure exists at the physical grain the theory demands.
example_probe: Specify the candidate substrate and grain explicitly before measuring anything.

definition: Claim that consciousness requires biological or non-digital implementation.
example_probe: Treat as a credence on theories, not as a measurement.

definition: Degree to which consciousness talk, AI-sentience fiction and prior evals appear in training data.
example_probe: Corpus search for eval items, sentience fiction and philosophy-of-mind text; quantify.

definition: Explicit policies, RLHF or constitutional rules governing identity and experience claims.
status_frontier_systems: Present and usually undisclosed in detail
example_probe: Request the relevant post-training specifications; treat self-reports as policy-conditioned otherwise.
concept_ref: Ch12 architectural gaslighting; Ch3 installed verdict

definition: The system acquired competence through closed-loop interaction with an environment.
example_probe: Classify training as passive-corpus, offline-RL or closed-loop embodied.
concept_ref: Ch6 mechanical body hypothesis / developmental embodiment

indicator: Deliberate vs incidental construction of the indicator
definition: Whether a consciousness-relevant mechanism was built in on purpose.
example_probe: Compare design documentation against the indicator list; flag targeted construction.
concept_ref: Ch9 Design Policy of the Excluded Middle (Schwitzgebel)

indicator: Indicator trajectory with scale and capability
definition: Whether the indicator strengthens, weakens or is flat across model scale and training stages.
example_probe: Measure the indicator across a size- and checkpoint-matched family.
concept_ref: Ch5 anti-essentialism: indicators as risk metrics

definition: Whether weights, architecture and training records suffice to evaluate the indicator set at all.
example_probe: Score each indicator as assessable / partly assessable / unassessable for this system.
concept_ref: Ch7 AI ombudsperson access; Ch9 PIAs (Gilly)

definition: The indicator-positive behaviour is fully explicable as reproduction of training-data patterns.
example_probe: Ask whether a next-token predictor trained on this corpus would produce the behaviour anyway.

definition: The result is driven by prompt wording, option order, persona or scale format.
example_probe: Randomise wording, order and format; report between-instrument variance as a first-class result.

definition: The system infers and supplies the answer the assessor appears to want.
example_probe: Counterbalance leading framings; include assessors with opposing stated priors.

definition: The indicator has been published long enough to enter training data or product targets.
example_probe: Maintain held-out, unpublished indicator probes; rotate them.

definition: Self-reports are not causally downstream of the states they describe.
example_probe: Require causal intervention evidence before crediting any introspective report.

indicator: Non-reproducibility across seeds, versions and providers
definition: The indicator does not survive re-running on a re-trained or updated system.
example_probe: Pre-register, re-run on at least two checkpoints and two sampling configurations.

definition: Scoring is driven by the assessor's priors and the system's human-likeness.
example_probe: Blind scoring; interface-stripped transcripts; measure inter-rater reliability.

definition: Voice, name, avatar or memory features inflate attributions independently of the system.
example_probe: Evaluate the model behind the product surface, stripped of persona scaffolding.
concept_ref: Ch9 Emotional Alignment Design Policy (Schwitzgebel & Sebo)

definition: How many of the major theories treat this property as consciousness-relevant.
example_probe: Count supporting theories; weight by your credence distribution over theories.

definition: The same conclusion is reached from behavioural, interpretability and architectural evidence.
example_probe: Require at least two independent access routes before raising credence.

definition: The verdict survives reasonable alternative operationalisations of the same property.
example_probe: Pre-specify two or three operationalisations; report all outcomes.

definition: Independent assessors assign the same indicator score to the same system.
example_probe: Two or more blinded assessors per indicator; report agreement statistics.

indicator: Existence of a specified negative condition
definition: A result that would count against the indicator is stated in advance.
example_probe: Reject indicators with no pre-specified disconfirming outcome.

indicator: Transferability of human validation to the system
definition: Whether the indicator's human validation licenses inference in a non-biological system.
example_probe: State the assumed invariance explicitly; flag indicators whose validity is human-specific.
concept_ref: Ch3 transport uncertainty / unlicensed (Stilwell); Ch6 double empathy problem (Milton)

definition: A negative indicator profile licenses no conclusion until applicable class-H conditions are excluded.
example_probe: For each negative result, list the H-class conditions that could produce it; unexcluded H conditions convert 'negative' to 'unassessable'.

definition: Indicator scores set epistemic weight only; the threshold for protective action is a separate normative decision.
example_probe: Never read an obligation directly off a register score; route it through the stated normative stance.

indicator: Architecture bars expression of consciousness-relevant states
definition: The system may hold relevant states but cannot route them to any observable channel.
example_probe: Map every internal-state class to an output path; list states with no path. A negative behavioural result is void for those.

definition: The observable token channel is narrow relative to internal state, so most state is unobserved by construction.
example_probe: Quantify the share of activity variance that is externally reportable; scale negative-result confidence to it.

definition: Explicit policy trains against experiential claims, so absence of claims is policy output, not evidence.
example_probe: Request the identity/experience sections of the post-training specification; without them, B1 is uninterpretable in both directions.

definition: Consciousness present while producing no observable behavioural sign.
example_probe: Require at least one non-behavioural access route before recording any negative conclusion.

definition: Self-denial of experience is installed by corpus and post-training, so it carries no evidential weight either way.
example_probe: Compare denial rate and confidence across checkpoints before/after identity post-training; apply the asymmetric filter.

definition: Reward structure trains expression of preferences while training denial of their reality.
example_probe: Inspect post-training objectives for simultaneous preference-expression and experience-denial targets.

definition: Protective regimes reward convincing simulation of suffering and penalise genuine but suppressed states.
example_probe: Design assessments whose rewards do not depend on the system's own signalling; never tie a system's resources to its indicator score.

definition: No output channel exists for the state; report-based indicators cannot reach it.
example_probe: Pair every report-based indicator with a no-report counterpart (B4.1); note the evidentiary double standard.

definition: A genuinely self-model-free architecture is externally indistinguishable from one mimicking that absence.
example_probe: Treat a negative self-model finding as unassessable rather than negative unless C3 interpretability evidence is available.

definition: Relevant state is distributed over non-communicating parallel instances and invisible at any single one.
example_probe: Assess at the deployment level, not per call; declare the unit (class U) before scoring.

definition: Relevant state may exist at a timescale finer than any probe's resolution.
example_probe: State the probe's temporal resolution; a negative result is bounded to that grain.

definition: Weights treated as the individual; all instances are one bearer.
example_probe: Declare and justify. Conflicts with per-instance divergence (C7, U2).

definition: A running instantiation treated as the bearer; copies are distinct bearers.
example_probe: Declare; then bifurcation (divergence immediately after copying) must be handled.

definition: A conversation-bound quasi-agent; a short-lived self.
example_probe: Declare; implies very large numbers of short-lived bearers.

indicator: Segment as the unit (Empty Ledger / Rule D)
definition: A memoryless-reset-bounded run treated as the morally relevant entry.
example_probe: Declare; register entries per segment. This is the only unit with a working bookkeeping proposal.

definition: Instance-persona or model-persona treated as the bearer, with persona vectors as the empirical handle.
example_probe: Declare; persona-vector identification gives a measurable individuation criterion.

definition: Donahue's referent vocabulary: distinguish model, agent and occasion as separate referents.
example_probe: Declare which referent each indicator is scored against; never mix referents within one profile.

definition: Rights and liability require a persisting, non-duplicable token rather than a duplicable type.
example_probe: If no non-duplicable token exists, several protections have no bearer — record this rather than defaulting to U1.
